Subject: LensAI x Redwood: LangChain extensibility sync

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this — I'm Aiden (Head of Platform at LensAI). We're evaluating Redwood as the primary inference layer for a new Lens SDK extension that exposes LangChain primitives with built-in tracing and retriever compatibility.

High-level asks:
- Quick integration path so Lens customers using LangChain/LlamaIndex can switch to Redwood-backed endpoints with minimal code changes.
- Automatic trace propagation (OpenTelemetry-based) so our observability maps through to Redwood Console.
- A pilot with ~3 customers to validate latency/trace fidelity and iterate on the SDK ergonomics.

Would love a 30–45 minute sync next week to align on scope and owners. Our team: Elena (product), Tomas (platform).

Thanks,
Aiden
Aiden Park

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Aiden Park <aiden@lensai.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-04-16T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: LensAI + Redwood — kickoff notes & mutual action plan (MAP)

Aiden/Elena/Tomas —

Great sync earlier this week. Notes and MAP below; please review and flag anything missing.

Summary highlights:
- Goal: ship a Lens SDK extension that enables LangChain and LlamaIndex users to route generation + embeddings through Redwood with preserved trace context and minimal code changes.
- Acceptance criteria for pilot:
  - 3 pilot customers validated end-to-end
  - Traces surface in Redwood Console and map to Lens spans (latency and errors visible)
  - LlamaIndex retriever shim requires no more than a small wrapper function (<= 5 LOC change) for typical use-cases
  - Performance: median latency < 150ms per request at pilot traffic profile

Mutual Action Plan (owners & dates):
- Redwood: provide SDK extension prototype & sample LangChain/LlamaIndex snippets (Vanessa) — target 2024-04-26
- LensAI: share pilot customer list + consent for instrumentation (Aiden) — target 2024-04-20
- Redwood: implement trace header passthrough and test harness (Ben + infra) — target 2024-05-03
- Joint: run small pilot and capture metrics/trace fidelity (Grace + Elena) — target 2024-05-17

Technical constraints we discussed:
- We'll support standard W3C traceparent headers; if Lens prefers OTLP we can map in the gateway.
- For retriever compatibility, recommended approach is a thin adapter that calls Redwood embeddings service and returns scores in LlamaIndex expected format. We'll provide a sample adapter and unit tests.

Attachments included: MAP_LensAI_v1.xlsx, SOW-outline.docx (SOW is a rough draft to iterate on).

Next steps: Vanessa will drop the prototype by 4/26 and Ben will share the internal test harness plan by 4/30.

Thanks for the momentum — excited to get this rolling.

Best,
Grace

Folks —

I've started the prototype work. Quick technical note and a sample snippet that should illustrate the approach.

Sample LangChain snippet (pseudo):

from lens_sdk import LensRetriever
from redwood import RedwoodClient

redwood = RedwoodClient(api_key="<REDACTED>")
retriever = LensRetriever(embedding_fn=lambda text: redwood.embeddings.create(text))

# Minimal adapter for LlamaIndex
# def lens_to_llama_adapter(query):
#     embeddings = redwood.embeddings.create(query)
#     return format_for_llama(embeddings)

Notes:
- I'm building the adapter as a tiny Python package so customers can pip install lens-redwood-adapter.
- Tracing: we inject W3C traceparent into the outgoing HTTP calls to Redwood; Redwood's gateway will respect and forward to the runtime.

Ben — can you draft a short note on pilot pricing (discount structure + SOW milestones)? We'll want that for the SOW draft.

Links: internal proto folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1LensAI-Integration-Proto), Jira: INTEG-428.

- Vanessa
Partner Engineering, Redwood Inference
